newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks overcome weakness to hit new record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks overcome weakness to hit new record.

text.p: Swiss shares overcame early weakness to end at a new closing record, but still slightly off the all-time high of nearly 4,300 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
The U.S. dollar's strength, lively buying interest by foreign investors and prospects for low interest rates were seen as factors behind the rise.
Financial shares were sought, while Roche certificates saw a correction after their recent record run.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 10.6 points, or 0.25 percent, to 4,282.8 points. The high was at 4,298.3.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 8.93 points to 2,737.26.
Roche slumped 255 francs, or 2.04 percent, to 12,240 francs due to profit taking. Novartis added 21 francs to 1,650.
Financials saw generally good demand after a period of lagging behind the market, a trader noted.

Swiss Re powered ahead, added 31 francs, or more than two percent, to 1,433. UBS bearer shares firmed 12 francs to 1,193. CS Group and SBC gained 1.25 francs to 147.50 francs and four francs to 267, respectively.
Among industrial shares, ABB was one of the few winners with an advance of eight francs to 1,828.
